name: Barbell Hip Thrust
cues: Rest your upper back on the bench edge just below your shoulder blades
Pad the bar and roll it into your hip crease
Set your feet so your shins are vertical at the top
Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down
Lock out with your glutes, not by arching your lower back

qa.note: Approved by the owner 2026-10-01 (bulk approval of every pending exercise). Earlier findings, kept for follow-up: Family review 2026-10-01 rated needs work. review: Biomechanics are good: shins vertical at lockout, hips -4 to 75 deg (Brazil 75 +/- 19), knees 91 to 112, ribs down (lumbar never extends), chin tucked, back pivoting on the bench edge, bar and pad on the hip crease. The primary (glute_max) is almost invisible from the hero camera: only a red sliver under the shorts. I tested a low front camera (az -40, elev 0.12): it hides the torso and was worse, so I reverted it. The owner should judge glute visibility. | skeptic: The primary is not visible. glute_max is the only primary on 502, and in the hero figure-502.png it shows only as a thin red sliver under the shorts at t=0.5 to 0.75, with nothing at the top (t=0, t=0.875). The side sheet shows the same sliver. The only clearly highlighted muscle is the secondary (hamstrings, orange). The rubric treats a view that hides the primaries as needs_work, even though the biomechanics are good: shins about vertical at lockout, knees 91 to 112 deg, hips -4 to 75 deg, no lumbar extension, chin tucked (neck 22 to 34 deg), bar on the hip crease. | skeptic: The primary (glute_max) is effectively invisible in every frame and view. In refute-visual/figure-502.png the shorts show no glute tint, and at the bottom (t=0.5 to 0.75) the near plate covers the pelvis, leaving only a red sliver at the seat. refute-visual-side/figure-502-side.png is the same. The only clear highlight is the orange hamstrings (secondary) under the thighs, so a user reads this as a hamstring exercise. That fails DoD item 5 ('camera shows the primaries'). Biomechanics, feet (refute-visual-foot/figure-502-foot_R.png) and bench contact are fine.
